candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Solid activity, positive year-to-date equity trend, and upcoming macro data could maintain broad risk appetite.
evidence: S&P 500 closed July 31 up 0.7% on the day and was up 9.4% year to date.
SPY 21-session return was 0.17%, with a 63-session volatility of 13.64% and max drawdown of -4.49%.
FOMC held rates at 3.50% to 3.75% while describing inflation as elevated and outlook uncertainty as elevated.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if SPY breaks decisively below recent 63-session drawdown levels while rates and inflation expectations rise.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Elevated inflation, higher Treasury yields, weak payroll revisions, or disappointing mega-cap earnings could trigger a one-month pullback.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: July employment data, CPI/PPI, retail sales, Fed minutes, second GDP estimate, PCE, durable goods, and Nvidia results before August 31.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Lower volatility, shallow drawdown, and recent relative leadership support continued rotation into value if growth remains solid.
evidence: Large value had a 21-session active return of 3.09% and prior 105-session active return of 3.48%.
Its 63-session volatility was 11.74%, lower than SPY's 13.64%, and max drawdown was -2.40%.
Distance from 52-week high was only -0.09%, with quality evidence score of 0.616.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if value gives back its recent 21-day active leadership and breaks materially below its 52-week-high proximity while SPY breadth narrows.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: A renewed mega-cap growth rally or recession scare could reverse value leadership and favor SPY concentration.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: July CPI, retail sales, GDP revision, and personal income/outlays may support value/cyclical breadth if growth remains solid and rates stabilize.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Strong prior relative trend and cloud-spending signals can support cybersecurity if tech earnings remain constructive.
evidence: Cybersecurity had a 23.30% prior 105-session active return and 0.62% 21-session active return.
It was only -3.06% from its 52-week high, with a quality evidence score of 0.610.
Microsoft reported revenue up 18%, cloud revenue up 27%, and Azure growth of 43%, providing a cloud-spending read-through.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if tech earnings read-throughs disappoint or cybersecurity falls below recent relative strength versus SPY.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: High 63-session volatility of 32.35% and beta above SPY leave it vulnerable to growth-stock derating or earnings disappointment.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: August technology earnings read-throughs, especially AMD and Nvidia, plus broader cloud/software spending signals before month-end.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Supply disruption, unresolved geopolitical claims, and route-risk premium can keep crude firm through the one-month horizon.
evidence: Oil had a 24.91% 21-session active return and 22.47% prior 105-session active return.
June global oil supply was estimated 9.4 million barrels per day below its pre-war level, and Gulf exports were 16.1 million barrels per day versus 24 million before the war.
No agreement had been reached on Strait of Hormuz reopening statements as of the cutoff, and OPEC+ highlighted energy infrastructure and maritime-route risks.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if a credible reopening/agreement is confirmed and crude reverses below its recent breakout relative to SPY.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Recent 5-session oil return was -5.50%, volatility was 53.42%, and any credible reopening or de-escalation could unwind the geopolitical premium quickly.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: Unresolved Strait of Hormuz claims, Gulf export disruption, and OPEC+ September production adjustment decision before August trading concludes.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Near-high price action and positive recent active return support continuation if European inflation data do not worsen materially.
evidence: Europe had a 3.04% 21-session active return and was only -0.44% from its 52-week high.
Its 5-session return was 2.47%, and beta to SPY was 0.920.
The ECB kept its three policy rates unchanged, while final July euro-area inflation is scheduled within the scoring window.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if euro-area inflation or energy-price stress worsens enough to trigger renewed underperformance versus SPY.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Euro-area inflation at 2.9% and energy inflation at 10.0% could pressure margins, rates, and equity sentiment.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: Final July euro-area inflation and global risk appetite data may confirm acceptable inflation and support international equity flows.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: A rebound in semiconductor-linked risk appetite and upcoming Nvidia results could revive Taiwan's prior leadership.
evidence: Taiwan had the highest prior active rank at 1.000 and a quality evidence score of 0.757.
It had a 43.33% prior 105-session active return but -8.82% 21-session active return.
63-session volatility was 44.26%, beta was 1.779, and distance from 52-week high was -13.43%.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if Taiwan fails to recover relative to SPY after semiconductor earnings catalysts or makes new relative lows.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Large recent underperformance and high volatility suggest momentum damage could persist over only one month.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: Nvidia results and global electronics/AI sentiment before the August 31 close.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Cash-like yield and very low volatility support capital preservation if risk assets weaken.
evidence: Short Treasury had 0.08% 5-session return and 0.14% 21-session active return.
It had 0.21% 63-session volatility, zero 52-week-high distance, and shallow max drawdown of -0.01%.
FOMC maintained the federal-funds range at 3.50% to 3.75%.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated as an alpha candidate if SPY trend strengthens and short Treasury continues to lag risk assets.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: A positive equity month would likely leave short Treasury far behind SPY despite low drawdown.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: No specific upside catalyst beyond carry and any risk-off reaction to August macro data.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Higher yields, recent relative strength, and shallow drawdown could support banks and insurers if credit remains benign.
evidence: Financials had a 3.77% 21-session active return and -1.15% distance from 52-week high.
63-session volatility was 13.66%, close to SPY, and max drawdown was -2.42%.
FOMC kept rates unchanged, and the ten-year Treasury yield rose to 4.71%.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if yield-curve or credit-quality signals deteriorate and financials lose recent active leadership versus SPY.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Soft payroll revisions, slower GDP growth, or credit-quality concerns could hurt financials despite yield support.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: July employment, CPI, retail sales, Fed minutes, and personal income/outlays data before month-end.

key_risks: A broad risk-off move could cause all equity holdings to underperform SPY or decline together.
A confirmed Strait of Hormuz reopening or de-escalation could sharply reverse oil exposure.
Hot CPI/PCE data or hawkish Fed minutes could pressure equities and duration-sensitive valuation multiples.
Nvidia, AMD, or other technology earnings read-throughs could disappoint and weaken cybersecurity sentiment.

portfolio.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if value gives back its recent 21-day active leadership and breaks materially below its 52-week-high proximity while SPY breadth narrows.
portfolio.rationale: Large-cap value shows favorable relative performance with lower volatility and shallow drawdown versus SPY, offering a steadier active equity tilt for one month.
portfolio.time_window_catalyst: July CPI, retail sales, GDP revision, and personal income/outlays may support value/cyclical breadth if growth remains solid and rates stabilize.

portfolio.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if tech earnings read-throughs disappoint or cybersecurity falls below recent relative strength versus SPY.
portfolio.rationale: Cybersecurity combines strong prior active trend with moderate recent active outperformance and a near-high price position, while avoiding the most extreme semiconductor drawdowns.
portfolio.time_window_catalyst: August technology earnings read-throughs, especially AMD and Nvidia, plus broader cloud/software spending signals before month-end.

portfolio.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if a credible reopening/agreement is confirmed and crude reverses below its recent breakout relative to SPY.

portfolio.time_window_catalyst: Unresolved Strait of Hormuz claims, Gulf export disruption, and OPEC+ September production adjustment decision before August trading concludes.

portfolio.invalidation_condition: Invalidated if euro-area inflation or energy-price stress worsens enough to trigger renewed underperformance versus SPY.
portfolio.rationale: Europe is close to a 52-week high with positive recent active return, offering non-US equity diversification and a lower beta than SPY in the supplied context.
portfolio.time_window_catalyst: Final July euro-area inflation and global risk appetite data may confirm acceptable inflation and support international equity flows.

portfolio_rationale: The portfolio avoids a single concentrated bet and selects only active holdings with base forecasts above SPY. It balances value equity, cybersecurity growth, geopolitical oil optionality, and Europe while keeping every non-benchmark cluster at or below 25%.
rationale_summary: SPY has a positive but modest base case after a flat July and elevated inflation/rate uncertainty. The selected basket targets stronger one-month catalysts from value breadth, tech earnings, energy disruption, and international catch-up.
